log.a:
Python answer: it prints

[[0, 1], [0, 1]] [[0, 1], [0, 1, 2]] True

Why: [[0]] * 2 makes an outer list holding two references to the same inner list L. a.copy() is shallow, so b is a new outer list that still points at L twice. a[0] += [1] calls list __iadd__, which extends L in place (to [0, 1]) and then reassigns a[0] to that same L. Every slot in both lists sees the change. b[1] = b[1] + [2] uses plain +, which builds a brand-new list [0, 1, 2] and puts it only in b's second slot. a is untouched, and b[0] is still L. So a[0] is b[0] is True.

log.a:
Tuesday answer: 13/27.

Counting: each child is one of 14 equally likely (sex, weekday) types, so there are 14 × 14 = 196 ordered pairs. Pairs with at least one Tuesday-boy: 14 where the first child is one, plus 14 where the second is, minus 1 for double-counting (Tuesday-boy, Tuesday-boy), giving 27. Among those, both boys: the first is a Tuesday-boy and the second is any of 7 boy-days (7), plus the reverse (7), minus the shared case (1), giving 13. So 13/27, which is just under 1/2. The day detail matters because it makes the "at least one" condition close to identifying a specific child.

log.a:
The answer is 7,350.

Method: set the S's aside and arrange the other seven letters first. Those are M, I, I, I, I, P, P, which gives 7!/(4!·2!·1!) = 5040/48 = 105 arrangements.

Any arrangement of seven letters leaves 8 gaps: one before the first letter, six between letters, and one after the last. No two S's can touch, so each S needs its own gap. All the S's are identical, so we only choose which 4 of the 8 gaps get one: C(8,4) = 70.

Each choice of gaps produces a different word, so the total is 105 × 70 = 7,350.

As a sanity check, MISSISSIPPI has 11!/(4!·4!·2!) = 34,650 arrangements in all. So about 21% of them keep the S's apart.
